title: schema/link-clock.schema.json and message fixtures, validated in Rust and TypeScript
description:
## Intent
One contract for the clock messages between `apricity serve` (Rust) and the page (TypeScript).

## Steps
1. `schema/link-clock.schema.json` (draft 2020-12, like `sample-manifest.schema.json`): `clock` {tempo, beat, serverMicros, playing, peers, quantum, startStopShared}, `ping` {t}, `pong` {t, serverMicros}, `error` {message}. `additionalProperties: false`.
2. `features/link/fixtures/`: one valid example per message and a few invalid ones (missing field, wrong type, unknown type).
3. Validation in both suites: a Rust test in `crates/apricity-cli` validating what `serve` sends (the `jsonschema` crate if already in the workspace, else ask the reviewer before adding it); a TS test validating what `link-clock.ts` accepts.
4. Mention the schema in the README layout table's `schema/` row.

## Verify
`cargo test -p apricity-cli link_clock_schema` and `cd web && npx tsx --test test/link-clock.test.ts`.

Commit: `feat(<this task id>): link clock message schema`.

## Protocol
Specs first, watched red; log decisions, problems and outcomes with `kbs comment`; run Verify and paste the tail. Every Bash call starts `export PATH=$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH && cd /Users/home/Projects/Apricity`; cargo with `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 RUST_TEST_THREADS=2` under `safe-run.sh --`. Never change dependencies to make a build pass. Sub-agents never commit, push or close.
